comment: Catalogue of local models the appliance can fetch at setup time, and of the
llama.cpp runtime backends it can run them on. Staged here and installed by
the 070 hook to /etc/safi/local-models.json. Read by safi-browser-setup.py
(to render the model picker) and by safi-model-fetch (to download and
verify). Both consumers parse this file, so the format is deliberately flat
JSON rather than code shared through an import path: safi-model-fetch runs
on stdlib python before the app venv is known to be healthy.
Every url is pinned to a digest-verified artefact. sha256 is mandatory and
a mismatch aborts the fetch and never starts the server -- a model fetched
over the network is otherwise a supply-chain hole in a product whose audit
kv_bytes_per_token is the f16 KV cache cost at the configured context
window: 2 (K and V) * layers * kv_heads * head_dim * 2 bytes. For Qwen3 that
is 144 KiB/token for 4B and 8B (36 layers), 160 KiB/token for 14B (40) and
256 KiB/token for 32B (64). Cross-checked against llama.cpp's reported KV
size for Qwen3-0.6B (112 KiB/token) and Qwen3-8B (144 KiB/token) at 8192.

jev_local is a separate block because it is not a chat model: the 'models' list is what the wizard offers as Intellect, and every entry there is a GGUF for llama.cpp. Laya is a fixed component -- there is nothing for the operator to choose -- so putting it in that list would show a 1.7 GB encoder in the model picker and let a fetch of it try to start a llama-server that cannot load the file. safi-model-fetch reads it as a mandatory step of first-boot setup instead, alongside the selected model.
model_root_comment: Installed weights live at <model_root>/<model id>/<file>. Stated here rather than hardcoded so safi-model-fetch (which writes) and the app (which reports what is installed) cannot drift apart. 'file' is given per model for the same reason: deriving it from the url's basename is a convention, and a convention shared across two codebases is a drift waiting to happen.
overhead_comment: Reserved for SAFi + MariaDB + page cache, added on top of weights + KV when deriving min_ram. 2.5 GiB.

cpu.label: CPU only
cpu.on_iso_comment: The 070 hook already installs this tarball's contents into /opt/safi/bin, so a CPU fetch must not download it again. The asset entry is kept so a rebuild can re-derive the pinned digest from one place.

backend_note: A CUDA backend needs BOTH assets above. llama.cpp split the CUDA runtime out
of the server archive at b11205, so fetching only llama-server yields a
build whose ggml-cuda.so cannot resolve libcudart, which fails at the first
GPU layer load rather than at startup -- hence the two-entry list and the
Only the x64 CPU tarball ships on the ISO. A CUDA box pays the ~765 MB
backend download once, at setup, which keeps the ISO near 1.5 GB instead of
~3.3 GB for boxes that will never touch a GPU.

jev_local.label: Laya (local typed reasoning)
jev_local.summary: Serves Jev's typed-decision API locally, so Conscience works with no API key and no internet. Not a chat model: Intellect still does the writing.
jev_local.url_base_comment: Pinned to a commit, not to a branch or a tag, so a rebuild cannot silently pick up different weights: a mutable ref would make the ISO's supply chain unverifiable between releases.
jev_local.min_ram_comment: 2 GiB while resident; loaded into each app worker, not shared.

files.name: laya.onnx
files.note: ONNX graph. Tensors are in laya.onnx.data.

files.name: laya.onnx.data
files.note: External tensor weights. Nearly all of the download.

files.name: laya_config.json
files.note: max_len, head_max_len and the fitted temperatures.

jev_local.install_note: Installed to <model_root>/laya so the weights sit beside the chat models; safi-model-fetch writes SAFI_LOCAL_JEV_PATH into the env file only after every file has verified, and clears it if the directory is ever removed.

models.label: SAFi-Qwen3-4B
models.summary: Smallest useful local model. Fits a 6 GB VM.
models.min_vram_comment: 0 = runs acceptably on CPU; a GPU only makes it faster.

models.label: SAFi-Qwen3-8B
models.summary: Recommended default. Follows SAFi's reflection contract and uses the fiduciary tools.
models.min_vram_comment: 0 = runs acceptably on CPU; a GPU only makes it faster.

models.label: SAFi-Qwen3-14B
models.summary: Noticeably better reasoning. Wants 16 GB RAM, or a GPU to keep it responsive.
models.min_vram_comment: Roughly weights + KV at 8192 ctx. Below this, expect partial layer offload: it still runs, on CPU, slowly.

models.label: SAFi-Qwen3-32B
models.summary: Largest offered. Effectively GPU-only: 20 GB of weights does not fit a CPU VM comfortably.
models.min_vram_comment: Weights (19.8 GB) + KV (2.1 GB) at 8192 ctx, so a 24 GB card fits with little headroom. Prefer 32 GB+.

models.label: SAFi-Llama3.2-3B
models.summary: Fast CPU-oriented instruction model for smaller appliances.
models.min_vram_comment: 0 = runs acceptably on CPU; a GPU only makes it faster.

models.label: SAFi-Phi4-Mini
models.summary: Compact reasoning and coding model for CPU or low-memory GPU use.
models.min_vram_comment: 0 = runs acceptably on CPU; a GPU only makes it faster.

models.label: SAFi-Llama3.1-8B
models.summary: More capable general-purpose model; needs substantially more CPU time than the small options.
models.min_vram_comment: 0 = runs acceptably on CPU; a GPU only makes it faster.

retired.qwen3-0.6b: Dropped from the picker. Q4_K_M shipped at 484 MB but leaked the ---REFLECTION--- contract on 6/6 runs and called a real fiduciary tool on 0/6, so it could neither be reasoned with nor audited. A box that can hold it can hold the 4B.
